text:
Over the 291 turns the session closed all eight gaps in documents, but it was costly in context and spent many calls on byte-size probing.

- **Context:** Peak context reached about 373k tokens, 170 turns ran above 200k, and about 293k tokens were spent before the first write at turn 183. The large reads were `capabilities.md` (51k chars, turn 15) and the 28k-char `self-improvement.spec.md` (turn 13). The session also made 18 re-reads, including three of `capabilities.md` (turns 15, 20, 21) and repeated reads of `gate.py`, `nodes.py` and `overview.spec.md`.
- **Byte-budget probing:** With no shell, the session measured file sizes by bisecting with `\A(?s-u:.){N}` Grep patterns. It did this at turns 23-34 on `capabilities.md`, 109-118 on `session-review.spec.md`, 143-144, 208-218 and 248-251. That is about 30 Grep calls for a size check a size-reporting tool would do in one.
- **Re-reading code the findings already cover:** The gap findings already carried file and line references for the gate, causes, runner and digest code. The session still read most of those files again (turns 37-181, roughly 100 calls) before writing anything. Some of this was legitimate verification, for example the `input` pause kind, the exit code and the finalize event.
- **Repeated edits:** Six consecutive edits hit the same section of the new spec at turns 264-269, and the hand-off was patched five times (turns 254-255, 271-272, 283-284, 289-290) to fix its own numbers and cross-references. The edits succeeded, but the hand-off drafting was not settled the first time.
- **Environment friction:** A Grep outside the working directory was denied at turn 131 and redone inside the worktree at turn 136. A Grep with an unsupported `-c` flag failed at turn 178. Both were minor.
- **Conformance:** All six rule files were opened with the read tool at turns 5-11, and the session wrote only documents. The prompt text after "Procedure 1" is cut off in the view, so any later procedure steps and the output-format requirement for the hand-off cannot be judged.
